firmographic.name: Airtable
firmographic.company_description:
Airtable (Formagrid Inc) is a cloud-based connected apps platform that combines spreadsheet-style usability with a relational-database architecture, enabling non-technical users to build custom business applications, automate workflows, and orchestrate AI agents without code. The core product suite includes HyperDB (enterprise-scale database handling hundreds of millions of records), Omni (conversational AI app builder), Superagent (multi-agent orchestration launched January 2026), Airtable AI Field Agents, Interface Designer, Portals, Automations, and a public REST API with extensions SDK. Underlying the platform is support for multiple foundation models (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Meta Llama), AWS-native infrastructure, and integrations spanning Slack, Salesforce, Jira, Databricks, Snowflake, and Google Drive.

Airtable monetizes through tiered per-seat SaaS subscriptions (Free, Team at $20–24/user/month, Business at $45–54/user/month, custom Enterprise Scale) plus usage-based AI credit add-ons starting at $40/month for 20,000 credits. Distribution follows a hybrid product-led growth motion at the bottom of the market (freemium, self-serve, Airtable Universe template community) combined with enterprise field sales targeting accounts spending over $100k annually; sources indicate roughly 70% of ARR now derives from large-account conversions as of mid-2025. The customer base spans 500,000+ organizations, including half of the Fortune 1000, with named enterprise logos such as Netflix, Shopify, Time, JetBlue, Vimeo, Dropbox, and Code and Theory.

The company, founded in 2012 by Howie Liu (CEO) and headquartered in San Francisco (~833 employees as of 2025), has raised approximately $1.36 billion in total venture funding across rounds including a $735M Series F in December 2021 led by XN at an $11 billion valuation. Subsequent strategic actions have been oriented toward an AI-native transformation: acquisitions of Dopt (2024) and DeepSky (2025), the launch of App Library and HyperDB (2024), the Omni rebrand (2025), and the Superagent standalone product (2026). Airtable reported cash flow positivity in late 2024 and has been linked to IPO preparation, though current secondary valuations are estimated near $4 billion, materially below peak.
firmographic.company_description_short: Airtable (Formagrid Inc) operates a cloud-based connected apps platform combining spreadsheet usability with relational-database power, enabling teams to build AI-augmented custom business apps, automations, and multi-agent workflows without code. It serves 500,000+ organizations including half of the Fortune 1000 with a hybrid PLG-to-enterprise SaaS model.

recent_move.description: Rebranded as an AI-native platform and launched Omni, a conversational AI agent that builds and automates applications through natural language prompts.

Released Superagent, Airtable's first standalone multi-agent AI product priced $20–$200/month, built on the acquired DeepSky technology to orchestrate specialized agents producing charts, timelines, and strategy decks.
Acquired DeepSky (formerly Gradient) to integrate multi-agent AI orchestration technology powering the Superagent product.
Launched enterprise-grade AI platform capabilities App Library and HyperDB, scaling datasets beyond 100 million records to compete with Microsoft, Salesforce, and ServiceNow.
Acquired Dopt (onboarding/AI startup) and absorbed its engineering talent, accelerating AI product development including the Airtable Cobuilder.
Conducted a 27% workforce reduction (from ~900 to ~833) to refocus on enterprise clients, followed by CTO hire of ex-OpenAI executive David Azose to drive AI transformation.
Airtable has achieved cash flow positivity and is considering an initial public offering (IPO) next year, signaling potential readiness for going public.

leadership_change.title: CTO Appointment - David Azose

expansion_highlight.description: Superagent (Jan 2026) is the first standalone product priced $20–$200/month, signaling intent to monetize beyond seat-based subscriptions and expand into individual knowledge-worker / prosumer use cases outside the existing enterprise base.

AI-native pricing transition including AI credit add-on packs starting at $40/month for 20,000 credits overlays usage-based revenue on top of per-seat subscriptions, opening expansion within existing accounts via AI consumption.

Sustained M&A appetite, Dopt (Jul 2024) and DeepSky (Oct 2025), with additional acquisitions Balsa and Airplane in early 2024, indicates active platform consolidation to accelerate capability gaps in onboarding, internal tooling, and AI reporting.

EU data residency option and Australian regional support, combined with explicit GDPR/CCPA programs and UK GDPR compliance, position Airtable for deeper EMEA penetration, though operating_geographies still list only USA, GBR, AUS as disclosed markets.

Expansion beyond core product/marketing/operations into Sales, HR, Finance, and Design solutions pages signals pursuit of additional enterprise verticals competing more directly with Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday workflows.

Leadership additions including CTO David Azose (ex-OpenAI), and product leadership (Marta Pinilla Aguilar as CPO, Zach Felsenstein in Product Development Strategy) point to organizational buildout for AI-native delivery and category-creation.
